bio: Black Hawk was a revered Lakota chief known throughout the Great Plains for his wisdom in diplomacy and his unwavering commitment to his people during the turbulent years of western expansion. Born in the Dakota Territory, he witnessed the dramatic changes brought by settlers and worked tirelessly to preserve his people's way of life while seeking peaceful coexistence.

Sarah Jane McCoy was one of the first women to establish a trading post in the Dakota Territory. Strong-willed and resourceful, she built relationships with both settlers and Native American tribes, becoming a respected figure in the frontier community. Her trading post became a hub for news, supplies, and cultural exchange in the harsh wilderness.

Jake "Wild" Morrison started as a notorious outlaw riding with various gangs across the frontier, but a chance encounter with a frontier preacher changed his path. He hung up his guns, established a cattle ranch, and became known for his quick draw turned into quick wit. His colorful past made him a local legend and his redemption story inspired many settlers in the region.
